headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the costs of their dedicated grid infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Abigail Spanberger
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these billions of dollars in costs from falling on residential ratepayers. Governor Abigail Spanberger supported this decision, which is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing critical data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that data centers' water consumption be made public, addressing concerns about the industry's significant water use. Senator Kannan Srinivasan championed the bill, which aims to provide transparency and better inform public discourse on data center impacts.

headline: Local Control Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to require assessments of other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0567) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, local governments, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on homes and schools within 500 feet and allows localities to request assessments on water, agriculture, and historic resources. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
